salmon.label: Salmon search v1 (baby names)
notes: Ally 1998 → One Piece is almost certainly wrong: the likely cause is the TV series Ally McBeal (1997), which the linker did not reach (right year, wrong work). Real-person and TV-driven surges are the known gap of v1.

Game of Thrones names (Khaleesi, Arya, Daenerys) link only to the 1996 books, not the 2011 TV series, so their chance-match is weak (21%): a data gap in how the characters are linked, not a real miss.

paths.label: Reader paths v1 (Wikipedia Clickstream)
notes: The click-through is real but small: 0.4–1.3% of the readers who reached Roman numerals in February came straight from a Super Bowl article. Most of the February rise arrives from search, which fits people seeing "LVIII" on screen and looking it up. (August is also school holiday, so part of the gap is seasonal.)

Arabic numerals has its own relay: the Super Bowl 50 article, which explains the one year the NFL dropped Roman numerals, sends 500–1,455 readers there every February. That explains why Super Bowl 50 itself scored high in the timing test.

Across all the named ripples the same lesson holds: most of the extra attention comes by search, not by clicking a link. Direct clicks carry about 1–3% (Queen's Gambit → Chess, Chernobyl → the disaster).
Space → Speed of light shows no reader path at monthly resolution (Parker 54 clicks, Voyager 2 18, Chandrayaan-3 0). The Artemis I article had a different title in November 2022, so its row is empty.
